methodology: The study optimized electrospinning parameters including solvent ratio, flow rate, and applied voltage to achieve table jet formation and uniform fiber morphology under green conditions (DMC and acetone).
research_objective: To develop a sustainable and biocompatible green binary solvent system for PLA nanofiber electrospinning process optimization.

key_findings.finding: DMC-based solvent system enables a sustainable and potentially biocompatible route for the fabrication of medical scaffolds, considering the low toxicity of the employed solvents.
Electrospinning of PLA using a fully green binary solvent system based on DMC and acetone can provide a sustainable and biocompatible alternative to conventional toxic solvents.
The optimized electrospinning parameters resulted in continuous, bead-free nanofibers under ambient conditions.

DMC-based binary solvents can support PLA electrospinning under appropriately selected conditions, offering a sustainable and bio-compatible alternative to conventional toxic solvents while maintaining control over fiber morphology and structural properties.
Environmental conditions (temperature and relative humidity) influence jet solidification and fiber morphology during electrospinning.
Systematic variation of applied voltage and flow rate allowed identification of stable spinning conditions for continuous fibers.

Conclusions A green and sustainable electrospinning process for PLA was successfully devel- oped using DMC as a biodegradable solvent in combination with acetone as a volatile co-solvent. Solubility and phase-stability tests identified PLA 4043D as the only grade capableofforminghomogeneousandstablesolutionsinDMC/acetonemixturesacross a broad composition range. The electrospinning parameters were optimized stability tests identified PLA 4043D as the only grade capableofforminghomogeneousandstablesolutionsinDMC/acetonemixturesacross a broad composition range. The electrospinning parameters were optimized to ensure stablejetformationanduniformfiberdeposition,identifyingaPLA/DMC/ACsolution (9/45.5/45.5 wt%) processed at 0.5 mL·h−1 and 15 kV as the most effective conditions. Under these optimized conditions, continuous and bead-free nanofibers with mean di- ameters of ~1 µm were produced. SEM analysis revealed a uniform nanoscale surface porosity generated by the differential evaporation rates of DMC and acetone. For the aforementionedconditions,XRDandDSCmeasurementsconfirmedthepredominantly amorphousnatureofthefibers,withcrystallinitydecreasingfrom~44%inthepelletsto ~12%intheelectrospunmats. Mechanicaltestsperformedonthehighlyporousstructures (porosity ~ 78%) yielded an average tensile strength of 2.96 ± 0.40 MPa and an elastic modulusof66.66±16.47MPa. Overall,theseresultsdemonstratethatDMC-basedbinarysolventsystemscanreliably supportPLAelectrospinning,providingalesstoxicandmoresustainablealternativeto traditionalchlorinatedsolventswhileensuringstableprocessingandhighfiberquality.
